title: Product Test Lifecycle
purpose: Defines deterministic lifecycle resolution for the generic product implementation-test surface, including honest zero-applicable behavior and failure distinction.

normative_requirements.text: `product/scripts/test-product` shall resolve product implementation-test lifecycle state from `product-test-applicability` before reporting product-test success.
When applicability is zero-applicable, `product/scripts/test-product` may complete successfully only after validating the deterministic evidence that establishes legitimate zero-applicable state.

A successful zero-applicable result shall mean that no governed applicable product implementation-test obligation exists for the current repository state. It shall not mean that expected tests were unavailable, undiscovered, uninstalled, unexecutable, or skipped because of an execution failure.

When applicability is applicable-and-resolved, `product/scripts/test-product` shall execute every governed applicable product implementation-test obligation selected by the accepted applicability evidence and shall fail if any required applicable obligation fails.

When accepted authority indicates applicable product-test obligations but the corresponding governed tests cannot be resolved, lifecycle resolution shall fail with a distinct expected-but-undiscovered or unresolved-applicable classification rather than report zero applicable.

Missing stable interface capability, missing required runtime dependency, broken discovery or registration processing, malformed applicability evidence, and test execution failure shall remain failure classes distinct from legitimate zero-applicable state.

The product-test lifecycle shall produce deterministic obligation selection and execution ordering for equivalent accepted authority and repository state. The exact ordering algorithm is not prescribed by this contract.

The lifecycle result shall provide enough machine-usable classification to distinguish successful zero-applicable, successful applicable execution, failed applicable tests, unresolved expected tests, applicability-invalid evidence, interface/dependency failure, and execution infrastructure failure. Exact serialization and diagnostic wording remain implementation-defined.

Changing from zero-applicable to one or more applicable governed product tests shall not require redesign or repository-class-specific modification of common validation orchestration; common orchestration shall continue invoking `product/scripts/test-product`.

This lifecycle contract shall not define concrete product test suites, exact registration or discovery architecture, activation event syntax, test runner or framework selection, exact exit-code numbering beyond success versus failure, or product-specific test semantics.

conformance.rationale: Current accepted repo-spec authority declares no governed generic product implementation-test obligation for this requirement at product/scripts/test-product; source-development tests and validation self-tests are separate surfaces. Future activation requires a governed correspondence update.
